accepted_claims: Projection monotonicity: if P is a linear image of Q, then xc(P) ≤ xc(Q).
Every full-dimensional d-polytope with n ≥ d+2 distinct vertices is the coordinate projection of a full-dimensional inscribed (d+1)-polytope with exactly n vertices.
The explicit height-sign choice guarantees full dimension without a generic-position assumption or an additional vertex.
The simplex case n=d+1 cannot satisfy that dimension-raising conclusion and is handled separately by xc(P) ≤ d+1.
The inscribed and unrestricted square-root assertions, each quantified over every fixed dimension, are equivalent with a one-dimension shift and dimension-dependent constants.
An inscribed dimension-three square-root bound would imply the unrestricted polygon square-root bound; the established inscribed dimension-two theorem does not give this implication.
For each prescribed cap radius 0 < θ < π/2, at least n−1 lift vertices can lie in that cap on the unit sphere while a scaled coordinate map recovers the original P.
